bodies.intuition: Sometimes the batch size a run needs does not fit in memory. Gradient accumulation runs several smaller batches, adds their gradients together, and only then takes a step — the same update as one large batch, spread over several forward passes.
bodies.engineer: Skip the optimizer step for k micro-batches and divide the accumulated gradient by k. It buys effective batch size at the cost of wall-clock, and is not free with normalization layers whose statistics are computed per micro-batch rather than over the whole effective batch.
bodies.math: g = (1/k)Σ_{i=1..k} ∇L_{B_i}, then one step. Mathematically identical to a batch of size k|B| for the gradient, but not for anything computing batch statistics inside the forward pass.

emphasis.intuition: the same update as one large batch

viz.caption: Share of memory the activations take against everything else held during a step. Drag the micro-batch count to watch peak memory fall while the step takes longer.
